title: Micelle chemoton with two catalyst kinds: do micelle lineages breed true for their catalyst, or does the catalyst jump between micelles through the bath?
summary: In the micelle chemoton (20261025T0936-c02-micelle-chemoton-sighting) micelles grow and divide only on amphiphile made by the catalyst they hold, and a colony spreads from a few ignited micelles. Whether the catalyst is inherited at fission or leaks to neighbours decides whether this world can carry heredity. Partition strength sets the ignition fraction (chi=-3: a few ignite; chi<=-4.5: all ignite), so leakage and ignition are coupled.
experiment: Fork the micelle chemoton world with two catalysts K1, K2 that share the precursor and differ only in amphiphile yield (r2 = 1.3 r1), seeded as two random white-noise fields (K0=0.01 each) at chi=-3, dK=0.08. 2 seeds x 2 arms (r2 = 1.3 r1 and an identical twin r2 = r1), T=800, 128^2 (~6 min per run). Per micelle per frame, record its K1/K2 majority; count conversions of intact micelles (majority flips with no split) against off-kind daughters at splits; then K2 share by micelle count against the twin. A second arm with chi=-4.5 (all ignite) tests whether stronger partitioning lowers conversions.
